It adds no trust claims, attestation or authorization policy, endpoint, or deployment assertion. It does not touch the TB-011, TB-002 or T-053 boundaries and makes no qualification or activation claim. Only the README was visible, so the link target is unverified; a missing file would be a documentation issue, not a security one. The retired-record and external immutable links are unchanged context lines.

For provider-swift/Sources/ProviderBenchmark/SchedulerPrefillBenchmark.swift, only the metadata and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied, with no base_text or head_text unit. It is a benchmark tool, not the provider serving path. The visible hunks bump the report schema version from 4 to 5 and add optional prefillChunkTokens and maxBatchedTokensPerStep fields. The excerpt also shows the changed ranges extending to later lines, so I could not inspect those edits. Nothing visible touches the coordinator WebSocket, App Attest, key custody, encrypted prefix-cache storage or the fan helper.

The remaining question concerns the unseen benchmark changes: whether they alter production engine constants, defaults for prefill geometry or media limits, or memory admission. The README describes a Gemma 4 2,048/4,096 prompt geometry and a GPT-OSS and dense Qwen opt-in. If the full PR changes production engine or admission paths, those files fall under TB-007 and T-029 and need their own review. That is outside this batch. No concrete regression is supported by the visible evidence, so I return no findings and flag the limited coverage.
